mode: Prototype Discovery Engine: deterministic workflows; Gemini is not used. Python computed these exported results in advance; the browser selects them.
disclosure: Prototype Discovery Engine — this demonstration uses deterministic investigation workflows to represent the planned retrieval-augmented scientific analysis architecture. Scientific results shown are derived from verified project data where available.
source: NASA Terra/MODIS MOD11C3.061 monthly nighttime land surface temperature (LST_Night_CMG), 0.05 deg grid, LP DAAC, doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD11C3.061; data version phoenix-qc-v1.0
limits: Nighttime land surface temperature is not air temperature. These historical observations are not forecasts and do not establish causes. Seasonal test p-values assume independence; temporal dependence can affect significance. Ranking slopes does not test their differences.
unsupported_message: This prototype supports hidden-pattern discovery, regional ranking, local-versus-regional comparison and acceleration investigations. Try a suggested question. Only Phoenix, 2003–2024 is supported. Hottest is different from fastest warming.
method_note: Ranking and comparison use stored seasonal Mann–Kendall / seasonal Sen's slope results. Monthly slopes are multiplied by 12 for °C/year. Evidence Challenger recomputes this same validated method on two January-aligned periods; it does not test acceleration. Missing observations remain gaps.

investigations.label: Find a hidden warming pattern
investigations.question: Find a warming pattern that regional averages might hide.
investigations.title: Cell r10_c13 vs. Phoenix study area southeast · 2003–2024
investigations.finding: Cell r10_c13 (33.275°, -111.725°) has an estimated trend of 0.186 °C/year, versus 0.107 °C/year for Phoenix study area southeast. The estimated difference is +0.079 °C/year.

metadata.Study area: Phoenix fixed study window; not city boundaries
metadata.Method: Seasonal Mann-Kendall test (12-month period) with seasonal Sen's slope

tools: load_evidence(): validated committed regional results
retrieve_cells(): verified manifest hash, cell metadata and full calendars
calculate_cell_trends(): seasonal Mann–Kendall / Sen's slope for eligible cells
select_cell(): largest estimated cell-minus-containing-region slope difference
Evidence checks: units, coverage, and comparison-test availability
Plotly: generated chart from retrieved data; missing observations remain gaps
investigations.challenge: This cell was selected after scanning eligible cells for the largest slope difference. Selection and multiple comparisons make this exploratory. Cell and regional series overlap. Individual trend p-values do not test their difference; no spatial-dependence or multiple-testing correction is applied.
investigations.conclusion: Exploratory candidate for deeper investigation; a significant slope difference is not established.
investigations.matters: Regional summaries can conceal spatial variation worth investigating.

investigations.title: Regional warming rates · 2003–2024
investigations.finding: Phoenix study area southeast has the highest estimated warming rate: 0.107 °C/year. This ranking does not establish statistically significant regional differences.

investigations.label: Has Phoenix warming accelerated?
investigations.question: Has Phoenix warming accelerated since 2014?
investigations.title: Evidence Challenger · Phoenix · 2003–2024
investigations.finding: Verdict: Inconclusive — additional statistical testing required. Separate seasonal trend estimates do not prove acceleration. No slope-change test or uncertainty interval is implemented.

metadata.Method: Seasonal Mann-Kendall test (12-month period) with seasonal Sen's slope

tools: load_evidence(): validated committed regional results
Split observations into January-aligned 2003–2013 and 2014–2024 periods
run_trend(): recomputed seasonal trends without dropping missing positions
Evidence checks: units, coverage, and comparison-test availability
Plotly: generated chart from retrieved data; missing observations remain gaps
investigations.challenge: Two different estimated slopes do not, by themselves, prove that the warming rate changed.
investigations.conclusion: INCONCLUSIVE — an appropriate slope-change test is required before claiming acceleration.
investigations.matters: Challenging an attractive interpretation helps prevent unsupported conclusions.
